member.name: P:Ansys.ACT.Automation.Mechanical.AnalysisSettings.ANSYSAnalysisSettings.OutputSelection
member.summary: Gets or sets the Output Selection property in the Output Controls group of Analysis Settings.

member.summary: Makes sure one of this bolt pretension's fields is ready to use. This method should be called before the first read or write operation on any of the fields of this load. Using the GUI, it appears that Mechanical does not initialize the load until it is changed for the first time. Its input values are not consistent with the steps defined in the analysis settings (neither in count nor in value). Using the load in the uninitialized state leads to strange behaviour and wrong values.

member.name: P:Ansys.ACT.Automation.Mechanical.BoundaryConditions.Convection.FilmCoefficient
member.summary: Property used to get and set the film coefficient data The setter allows the use of a table object, an expression contained in a string or a quantity object as a data source. Depending on the representation type, the getter return type is a field object or an object which type depends on the source of the film coefficient data: - On table assignment mode, it returns the source table object. - On function mode, it returns a string containing the expression evaluated to obtain the data. - On constant mode, it returns a quantity object containg the value and the units currently assigned to the film coefficient. - On tabular mode, it returns a tabularDataTable object.

member.name: P:Ansys.ACT.Automation.Mechanical.BoundaryConditions.Convection.AmbientTemperature
member.summary: Property used to get and set the ambient temperature data The setter allows the use of a table object, an expression contained in a string or a quantity object as a data source. Depending on the representation type, the getter return type is a field object or an object which type depends on the source of the ambient temperature data: - On table assignment mode, it returns the source table object. - On function mode, it returns a string containing the expression evaluated to obtain the data. - On constant mode, it returns a quantity object containg the value and the units currently assigned to the ambient temperature. - On tabular mode, it returns a tabularDataTable object.

member.name: P:Ansys.ACT.Automation.Mechanical.MeshWorkflowOutput.LabelsExcludeFilter
member.summary: Gets or sets the regular expression to match all labels that are excluded from the transfer. The exclude match removes also labels matching the include pattern. Applies when "TransferLabelsAsNamedSelections" is True.
member.example: """The filter regular expressions support the same grammar as the scope pattern expressions, a few typical examples:""" 'abc.*' matches all names starting with 'abc'. '.*abc.*' matches all names containing 'abc'. '.*abc|.*xyz' matches all names ending with 'abc' or 'xyz'. More complex expressions, following the regular expressions grammar, are supported.

member.name: P:Ansys.ACT.Automation.Mechanical.MeshWorkflowOutput.LabelsIncludeFilter
member.summary: Gets or sets the regular expression to match all labels that are included in the transfer as Named Selections. Applies when "TransferLabelsAsNamedSelections" is True.
member.example: """The filter regular expressions support the same grammar as the scope pattern expressions, a few typical examples:""" 'abc.*' matches all names starting with 'abc'. '.*abc.*' matches all names containing 'abc'. '.*abc|.*xyz' matches all names ending with 'abc' or 'xyz'. More complex expressions, following the regular expressions grammar, are supported.

member.name: P:Ansys.ACT.Automation.Mechanical.MeshWorkflowOutput.TransferPrescribedPointsLabelsAsNamedSelections
member.summary: Gets or sets whether to configure the transfer of Prescribed Points labels to Mechanical as Named Selections. All labels defined on Prescribed Points will be transferred as criteria based Named Selections scoping the corresponding mesh nodes.

member.name: P:Ansys.ACT.Automation.Mechanical.MeshWorkflowOutput.TransferLabelsAsNamedSelections
member.summary: Gets or sets whether to configure the transfer of labels to Mechanical as Named Selections. If set to True, LabelsIncludeFilter must be set to define the whitelist of labels to be transferred, optionally LabelsExcludeFilter can be set to define a blacklist of labels to not be transferred. Only labels matching the LabelsIncludeFilter whitelist and not matching the LabelsExcludeFilter blacklist are transferred. This property is only visible when the DataTransferType is "ByTopology".

member.name: P:Ansys.ACT.Automation.Mechanical.Table.Column.IsFixedSize
member.remarks: The length of an individual load variation variable should not be changed in isolation. In other words, there may be sibling variables that _must_ have the same length. Thus, only the parent can be responsible for changing the length since all must be resized uniformly.

member.name: P:Ansys.ACT.Automation.Mechanical.Table.Column.VariableClassification
member.summary: Gets the variable classification of the columnar data.
member.remarks:
Some variable types, such as temperature or stress, can function as either independent or dependent variables. In such circumstances, will always return the dependent variable type.
Thus, it is important to check whether the variable is independent first. If yes, return directly. Otherwise, return the dependent classification.

member.summary:
Whether column add/create/import/refresh operations cannot grow the number of rows.
will always be `true` when is `true`.
When is `true`, any operation that would change the table row count will fail. This includes operations such as creating and adding a column, importing columns.

Creates and adds a new column (data series) to the table.
If `data` is provided, the number of rows (length of `data`) must be identical to the number of rows already in the table. If `data` is not provided, the returned series will have the same number of rows as the table with default-initialized values. If there are no rows in the table and `data` is provided, this will initialize the number of rows in the table to the length of `data`.

member.name: M:Ansys.ACT.Automation.Mechanical.Table.Import(System.String,Ansys.Mechanical.DataModel.MechanicalEnums.Table.ImportFormat,Ansys.Mechanical.Table.ImportSettingsBase)

summary.para: Import data from the provided resource into the table as specified by and . The column definitions in will be used to define the variable type for each column. If the table already contains a variable type, that column will be overwritten by the new definition.

When is true, will verify that the row count of imported data are equivalent to the existing table row count. The operation will fail if there is a length mismatch. Conversely, when is false, a Mechanical warning message will be issued when any of the data sources are different from each other or the table.
If all the arguments are `null` (Python: `None`) then the stored values will be used, essentially re-syncing the table data to the external sources.

member.remarks: All imported data in textual/string format will depend on the .NET `double.TryParse()` method to convert items into a suitable value for variable storage in the table. An “undefined” value (as specified in the `IDataTable` API spec) will be used if a suitable double representation cannot be parsed.
member.param: The URI of the data source to import.
The format of the data source.
The settings for how to import.
member.returns: A collection of the newly created columns.
member.exception: When an error occurred, likely due to missing data or incorrect import settings.
An unknown error occurred during import.

member.name: M:Ansys.ACT.Automation.Mechanical.Tree.Suspend
member.summary: Prevents the tree from being updated.
member.remarks: This method should be called before adding/removing objects to prevent multiple redraws. It should be used in association with a using/with block to ensure the Resume controller method to be called. Indeed, the Dispose method of controller automatically calls the Resume method.
member.example:
The following example add 10 comments below "Model" in one shot (without refreshing the tree for every add).
with(ExtAPI.DataModel.Tree.Suspend()): for i in range(10): ExtAPI.DataModel.Project.Model.AddComment()
Note: In C# one must use the "using" statement instead of "with"

member.name: M:Ansys.ACT.Automation.Mechanical.Tree.Find(System.String,System.Func{Ansys.Mechanical.DataModel.Interfaces.IDataModelObject,System.Boolean},System.String,Ansys.Mechanical.DataModel.Enums.ObjectState)
member.summary: Gets a list of all objects with the specified parameters.
member.param: The object's name.
The object's function.
The object's tag.
The object's state.
member.remarks: Note that all parameters of Find are optional. Name: Defaults to "" Func: Defaults to null Tag: Defaults to "" State: Defaults to ObjectState.NoState
member.example: The following command finds all objects with an state of Suppressed. ExtAPI.DataModel.Tree.Find(state=ObjectState.Suppressed)
The following command finds all objects with a name of "Force" and a tag of "Load". ExtAPI.DataModel.Tree.Find(name="Force", tag="Load")

The following command finds all objects with the name "Pressure", the function "defineByVector", the Tag "Test", and a ObjectState of Suppressed. def defineByVector(obj): if (obj.DefineBy == LoadDefineBy.Vector): return True return False ExtAPI.DataModel.Tree.Find(name="Pressure", func=defineByVector, tag="Test", state=ObjectState.Suppressed)

member.name: M:Ansys.ACT.Automation.Mechanical.Tree.Sort(Ansys.Mechanical.DataModel.Enums.SortingType,System.Boolean)
member.summary:
Sorts the tree objects based on given parameters. Type of sorting to apply. Wheter to sort in reverse order.
Note that all parameters of Sort are optional. type: Defaults to alphabetical reverse: Defaults to false
sorting in reverse order is currently not supported
Usage example - sort alphabetically ExtAPI.DataModel.Tree.Sort()
Usage example - sort alphabetically ExtAPI.DataModel.Tree.Sort(type=SortingType.Alphabetical, reverse=False)
Filters the tree objects based on given parameters.
member.param: Filter by a given name.
Filter by a given tag.
Filter by Suppression state.
Filter by Visibile/Invisible objects.
Filter by object Type.
Filter by Coordinate System scoping.
Filter by Model ("All", "Current", "Dropdown String").
Filter by Environment.
Filter by Scoping.
Filter by object State.
Filter by Property Name.
Filter by Property Value.
Flag to invert the search results.
member.remarks:
Note that the tree can be filtered by only one thing at a time, so a maximum of one parameter can be changed from its default value.
name: Defaults to "" tag: Defaults to "" state: Defaults to ObjectState.NoState visibility: Defaults to VisibilityType.All type: TreeFilterObjectClass.All coordinateSystem: None model: "All" environment: None scoping: TreeFilterScopingType.All filterState: TreeFilterObjectState.All propertyName: Defaults to "" propertyValue: Defaults to ""
member.example: The following example filters the tree for objects with a state of Suppressed. ExtAPI.DataModel.Tree.Filter(filterState=TreeFilterObjectState.Suppressed)
The following example filters the tree for objects with names who contain "Reaction". ExtAPI.DataModel.Tree.Filter(name="Reaction")
The following example filters the tree for objects that are visible. ExtAPI.DataModel.Tree.Filter(visibility=VisibilityType.Visible)
The following example filters the tree for objects that are part of the current model. ExtAPI.DataModel.Tree.Filter(model="Current")

member.name: M:Ansys.ACT.Automation.Mechanical.Tree.Group(System.Collections.IEnumerable)
member.summary: Groups a list of objects together.
member.param: The list of objects to group.
member.returns: The new group folder, otherwise throws an exception.
member.example: # Below are acceptable uses of Group folder = Tree.Group(Tree.ActiveObjects) folder = Tree.Group(Tree.FirstActiveObject) folder = Tree.Group([12,41,47,48,49,51,52,60]) analysis_18 = DataModel.GetObjectById(18) fixed_support_33 = analysis_18.AddFixedSupport() displacement_34 = analysis_18.AddDisplacement() frictionless_support_35 = analysis_18.AddFrictionlessSupport() folder = Tree.Group([ fixed_support_33, displacement_34, frictionless_support_35 ]) # (21,26) expands is short for object ids [21,22,23,24,25,26] dmo_list = DataModelObjectList([fixed_support_33, (21,26), 60] + [ dmo for dmo in Tree.ActiveObjects ]) folder = Tree.Group(dmo_list.Ids)

members.member:
Creates a new child Pressure. DataRepresentation.Field will use the Field object for working with tabular data DataRepresentation.Flexible allows the use of the following types when the pressure is defined as a normal to a surface: Quantity: The unit must be a valid Pressure unit string: It is interpreted as s table if it matches a Table name. Else it is interpreted as an expresion Table: A table object can be specified.
Returns the object created. """The following example creates a pressure on the first face of the first body for the first part.""" model = ExtAPI.DataModel.Project.Model pressure = model.Analyses[0].AddPressure() # Add a pressure. part1 = model.Geometry.Children[0] # Get the first part. body1 = part1.Children[0] # Get the first body. face1 = body1.GetGeoBody().Faces[0] # Get the first face of the body. selection = ExtAPI.SelectionManager.CreateSelectionInfo(SelectionTypeEnum.GeometryEntities) # Create an empty selection. selection.Entities = [face1] # Add the face to the selection. pressure.Location = selection # Assign the selection to the pressure. pressure.Magnitude.Inputs[0].DiscreteValues = [Quantity("0 [s]"), Quantity("1 [s]")] # Set the time values. pressure.Magnitude.Output.DiscreteValues = [Quantity("10 [Pa]"), Quantity("20 [Pa]")] # Set the magnitudes. "

member.name: M:Ansys.ACT.Common.Graphics.SymbolFactory.GetUnitSpring(System.Double,System.Double,System.Int32,System.Double,System.Double,System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary:
Creates a unit spring scenegraph node, aligned on the z axis going from z=0 to z=1. The spring tessellation is comprised of cylinder sections on each end, a coil in the center, and smoothed transition sections from the coil to the cylinder ends.
Examples: GetUnitSpring(0.01, 0.02, 5, 0.20, 0.05) # Short, thin spring bounded by long cylinder sections GetUnitSpring(0.01, 0.02, 25, 0.70, 0.05) # Long, thin spring bounded by short cylinder sections GetUnitSpring(0.02, 0.05, 10, 0.65, 0.10) # Thick spring bounded by short cylinder sections GetUnitSpring(0.01, 0.05, 25, 0.70, 0.05, 16) # Thin, widely coiled spring bounded by short cylinder sections
Note: tube_radius should generally be half (or less) the coil radius for nicer looking springs.
member.param: Radius of the tube comprising the spring.
Radius of the spring coil, measured from the center of the tube.
Number of turns of the spring coil. If less than 2, the spring will be represented as a cylinder.
Length of the spring coil section. Must be between 0 and 1.
Length of the spring transition sections (transitioning from the coil to the cylinder ends). Must be between 0 and 0.5, and spring_coil_length + 2 * spring_transition_length must not exceed 1.
Number of segments comprising each circle cross-section, higher values will rounder springs with more complex tessellation. Defaults to 8.
Number of segments used to transition from spring coil to cylinder ends, higher values will generate smoother transitions. Defaults to 5.

member.name: M:Ansys.ACT.Common.Graphics.SymbolFactory.GetUnitDamper(System.Double,System.Int32)
member.summary: Creates a unit damper scenegraph node, aligned on the z axis going from z=0 to z=1. A damper is represented by an inner tube surrounded by an outer tube with twice the radius.
member.param: Radius of the inner tube.
Number of segments comprising each circle cross-section, higher values will generate rounder dampers with more complex tessellation. Defaults to 8.

member.name: M:Ansys.ACT.Common.Graphics.MechanicalGraphicsWrapper.ExportViewportImage(System.Int32,System.String,Ansys.Mechanical.DataModel.Enums.GraphicsImageExportFormat,Ansys.Mechanical.Graphics.GraphicsImageExportSettings)
member.summary: Exports the current graphics display to a 2D image file.
member.param: An integer specifying the viewport. Valid values range from -1 to 3, depending the amount of viewports open. When two viewports are open side-by-side (horizontally), 0 refers to the left viewport and 1 refers to the right viewport. When two viewports are open and stacked (vertically), 0 refers to the top viewport and 1 refers to the bottom viewport. When four viewports are open, 0 refers to the top-left viewport, 1 refers to the top-right viewport, 2 refers to the bottom-left viewport and 3 refers to the bottom-right viewport. When -1 is passed in, the image is taken from the active viewport (equivalent to using Graphics.ExportImage). -1 is the only supported value in no-GUI mode.
The output image's file path. Non-existent directories will be created and pre-existing files will be overwritten. If null or empty, image will be copied to clipboard (Windows only)
The 2D image format to use when exporting.
The 2D image settings to use when exporting.

member.name: T:Ansys.ACT.Common.Post.ResultRepository
member.summary: Represents the result repository. It is aimed at being the main entry point for the core application to get result readers from result files, hiding the burden of the management of those readers (instanciation, caching and disposal) from the client code. For each result file, the reader code that actually deals with reading the file is hosted in a standalone process. Reusing the same reader as the one that Mechanical uses would lead to unpredictable failures because ACT would step on Mechanical toes.

member.name: T:Ansys.ACT.Interfaces.Mechanical.IRemovableDataModelObject
member.summary:
Interface for data model objects to implement if they support non-JScript removal.
Any pre- or post-removal actions can be supported by implementing one or both of and . If these methods are not sufficient, additional pre- or post-removal actions can be implemented in "CodeDV/DesignSpace/DSObjects/DSObjectsService.cpp" within the method `CDSObjectsService_ObjectCB(...)` under the checks for `pObjEvent->willErase()` and `pObjEvent->wasErased()` based on the DSObject's CLSID.
The overall process flow is:
CDSObjectsService_ObjectCB(...) -> willErase
Actual removal
CDSObjectsService_ObjectCB(...) -> wasErased

member.name: M:Ansys.ACT.Mechanical.Fields.Adapters.FieldAdapter.ChangeFieldDefinitionType(Ansys.Common.Interop.CAERepObjects.AnsBCLVType,Ansys.Common.Interop.AnsMaterial.kEDDataType)
member.summary: Changes the definition type for a field of the wrapped object from Mechanical.
member.remarks: The contract is the adapter is expected to raise a if the given definition type for its component is illegal. Mechanical does not support all definition types for all its field provider objects through its User Interface. Despite this, objects can get hacked by changing definition type programmatically, which would likely lead to unexpected behaviour from Mechanical.
member.param: Value that identifies the component of the wrapped object to change.
Value that corresponds to the new way to use for defining the component's values.
member.exception: The adapter does not support changing the definition of such component of the targeted boundary condition or the new definition type is not valid for the given component.

member.name: M:Ansys.ACT.Mechanical.Fields.Adapters.FieldAdapter.TryGetDiscreteValues(Ansys.ACT.Mechanical.Fields.Variable,System.Collections.Generic.IList{Ansys.Core.Units.Quantity})
member.summary: Tries to get the discrete values of the managed field.
member.remarks: This method should be useless in most cases since the general behaviour implemented by the variable - which consists in getting the underlying load variation - should suffice. However, some loads do have a specific behaviour (i.e. DSSpringAuto which has a property that could be either a Quantity or a Field).
member.param: Variable whose discrete values are to be gotten.
Output values to get.
member.return: true if this adapter took care of getting the discrete values, false if it did not touch the variable.

member.name: M:Ansys.ACT.Mechanical.Fields.Adapters.FieldAdapter.TrySetDiscreteValuesForOutput(Ansys.ACT.Mechanical.Fields.Variable,System.Collections.Generic.IList{Ansys.Core.Units.Quantity})
member.summary: Tries to set the discrete values for an output variable of the managed field.
member.remarks: This method should be useless in most cases since the general behaviour implemented by the variable - which consists in modifying the underlying load variation - should suffice. However, some loads do have a specific behaviour implemented in the DSObjects' boundary condition object (i.e. Hydrostatic Pressure). In such case, touching the load variation shunts this specific behaviour and we have to give the adapter a way to call the DSObject property instead.
member.param: Variable whose discrete values are to be changed.
Output values to set.
member.return: true if this adapter took care of setting the discrete values, false if it did not touch the variable.

member.name: M:Ansys.ACT.Mechanical.Fields.Variable.SetInternalDefinitionType(Ansys.Common.Interop.AnsMaterial.kEDDataType,System.Boolean)
member.summary: This is taken out from the InternalDefinitionType property since an argument must specify if the change to the other constant mode has been made. This avoids going into an infinite loop in the case where none of the constant value can be set. This has been seen in the Defect DE124211 for a ThermalCondition object, in which the first value for a constant ramped is the environment temperature (and not 0).
member.param: Specifies wether or not we must try to fallback to the other constant mode.

member.name: P:Ansys.ACT.Mechanical.Fields.Variable.DiscreteValues
member.summary: Gets or sets the discrete values of this variable or null if this variable represents a free degree of freedom.
member.remarks: Note that this collection of values can be discretized by Mechanical from the formula that defines this variable. Otherwise, if the variable is defined by a table of values, this property returns the values contained in the table.
member.exception: The property is set with a null value.
The property is set but the variable is an input variable which as a consequence cannot be modified.

The property is set with a list that does neither contain a single element nor as many elements than the input variables of the owner component. This type of exception can also be raised when setting the property from IronPython code, which allows passing a list containing integer values rather than floating point values. In that case, the issue can be worked around by adding a decimal point to each constant.

member.name: P:Ansys.ACT.Mechanical.Fields.VariableSignature.IntuitiveIndex
member.summary: Gets an index that reflects the position of the variable within its container load variation any Mechanical user would intuitively think of by looking at the GUI. For instance, the first variable in the "Independents" collection of a ILoadVariation object from Mechanical is wrapped by a signature that uses =0 since this is the actual position in the Independents collection. But for the user, this variable is the second independent variable, the first being the one returned by the "PrimaryIndependent" property of ILoadVariation. In this example, IntuitiveIndex would then return 1.
member.remarks: This index makes sense when speaking about a ILoadVariation but since this API wraps load variations in a more convenient manner, this property is not worth being exposed to the end-user. Indeed, it is not well suitable to output variables because whereas there can be several "Dependent" variables in a ILoadVariation object, there is always a single output per object, to remain consistent over the various types of load variations that can be encoutered in Mechanical (some use several outputs gathered in the same load variation while some other would use several load variations with a single output each). That is why even if it is more "intuitive" than can be, this index is still a bit too complex to grasp for the end-user.

The syntax required for Help Server commands is very simple. The syntax depends on the type of help you wish to display (e.g. help from ANSYS, Workbench, or Workbench 2). member.name: T:Ansys.ACT.Mechanical.Tools.SmartTextReader

summary.para: Read data from a text source file, attempting to determine the correct encoding. UTF-8 is the default encoding. The fall-back encoding is the system's default "ANSI" codepage, which will be used if all other supported encodings fail.

The class behavior is lazy, meaning it will not parse the source to detect the encoding until the encoding or decoded contents are requested. However, a correct encoding detection requires a full parse of the entire stream contents just in case the final character does not conform to UTF-8.

member.remarks: This is an adaptation of the approach provided in the Stack Overflow answer https://stackoverflow.com/a/52227667/18059257

member.summary: This method uses CreateRawTripleQuotedString and FormatOddNumberBackSlashesInRawString to prepare the right hand side of a string for journaling. It is currently used by CommandsController.
member.param: Original text.
member.returns: String that can be used in a python command for journaling.

member.name: M:Ansys.ACT.Mechanical.StringManipulationHelper.FormatDoubleQuotesInAStringForJournaling(System.String)
member.summary:
This method formats given string x in a way that any double quotes inside the string are not treated as raw string. We need this method to be used by the controller for Commands object, because we pass in the API command to be journaled to the commands layer using triple quotes and raw string identifier. In that case we don't want any triple quotes typed by the user to be treated as a raw string.
Ei. User types in "something is """ something", let this string be str, the commands controller receives "something is \"\"\" something" from the client. If we use this string as it is, in preparing the command to be journaled. We would write something like "cmd.Input = r\"\"\"something is \"\"\" something\"\"\"", in this case the triple quotes in str will not work because the command string that needs to be journaled wouldn't know which triple quotes are pairs, and we also don't want to treat the triple quotes as a raw string otherwise when the user uses the journaled command they would end up with backslashes in their text where there should not be.
In this case, we would want our command string to look something like this. "cmd.Input = r\"\"\"something is \"\"\" + "\"\"\"" + r\"\"\"" + something \"\"\"" Given the text = "something is \"\"\" something", this method will return - ["r\"\"\"something is \"\"\"", "\"\\\"\\\"\\\"\"", "r\"\"\" something\"\"\"] As it can been seen above the string is now split into multiple raw strings, and excludes the double quotes that the user typed.

member.name: M:Ansys.ACT.Mechanical.StringManipulationHelper.FormatOddNumberBackSlashesInRawString(System.Collections.Generic.List{System.String})
member.summary: This method simply extracts the last backslash into it's own string in a raw triple quoted string that ends with with odd number of backslashes. ei. r""" some string \\\""", this would not work because the last backslash is treated as an escape char for the first double quote. This method will turn the above string into r""" some string \\""" + "\\", which now has the same effect that was intended by original string but is correct in the python syntax.
member.param: List of raw triple quoted string generated using CreateRawTripleQuotedString
member.returns: List of strings where no raw triple quoted string ends with odd number of back slashes.

member.name: T:Ansys.ACT.WorkBench.Properties.ContractAnnotationAttribute
member.summary: Describes dependency between method input and output.
member.syntax:
Function Definition Table syntax:
FDT ::= FDTRow [;FDTRow]*
FDTRow ::= Input => Output | Output <= Input
Input ::= ParameterName: Value [, Input]*
Output ::= [ParameterName: Value]* {halt|stop|void|nothing|Value}
Value ::= true | false | null | notnull | canbenull
If method has single input parameter, it's name could be omitted.
Using halt (or void/nothing, which is the same) for method output means that the methos doesn't return normally.
canbenull annotation is only applicable for output parameters.
You can use multiple [ContractAnnotation] for each FDT row, or use single attribute with rows separated by semicolon.

item.code: [ContractAnnotation("halt <= condition: false")] public void Assert(bool condition, string text) // Regular Assertion method
[ContractAnnotation("s:null => true")] public bool IsNullOrEmpty(string s) // String.IsNullOrEmpty
[ContractAnnotation("s:null=>false; =>true,result:notnull; =>false, result:null")] public bool TryParse(string s, out Person result)

member.name: T:Ansys.Mechanical.DataModel.ConstructionLines.Utility.RollmarkAutomation
member.summary: This class is designed to be used to automate the creation of rollmarks for the engine. When used with a `using` statement, a rollmark may be created after the scope is exited. A rollmark is only created, however, if a call to `MarkCleanOperation()` has been made on the instance. Otherwise, the operation is treated as a failure and no rollmark will be attempted. This class cooperates with the `IAnsTransactionOperationTracker` from a DSConstructionLine instance to coordinate the generation of a single rollmark for an entire transaction. If no transaction has been started, it is expected that a rollmark will be created upon a clean call to `endOperation()`.

member.summary: A class that provides methods to apply mathematical Operations (like Integration, Summation, Multiplication, etc.) to dataset object(s). All operations throw an InvalidOperationException when an invalid dataset is passed in as an input. An invalid dataset could be null dataset reference, dataset with either of the x or y values list empty or dataset with a mismatch in the size of its x and y values list.

member.name: M:Ansys.Mechanical.DataModel.Utilities.Dataset.Operations.Integration(Ansys.Mechanical.DataModel.Utilities.Dataset.Dataset2D)
member.summary: Performs integration using the trapezoidal rule on a dataset and returns the result as a new dataset. The resultant dataset will be Dimensionless. (See documentation for more details) An ArgumentException is thrown if the input dataset is either invalid or contains less than two values.

member.name: M:Ansys.Mechanical.DataModel.Utilities.Dataset.Operations.Differentiation(Ansys.Mechanical.DataModel.Utilities.Dataset.Dataset2D)
member.summary: Performs differentiation using the central difference method on a dataset and returns the result as a new dataset. The resultant dataset will be Dimensionless. (See documentation for more details) An ArgumentException is thrown if the input dataset is either invalid or is non-differentiable.

member.name: M:Ansys.Mechanical.DataModel.Utilities.Dataset.Operations.Addition(Ansys.Mechanical.DataModel.Utilities.Dataset.Dataset2D,Ansys.Mechanical.DataModel.Utilities.Dataset.Dataset2D,Ansys.Mechanical.DataModel.Utilities.Dataset.Dataset2D[])
member.summary: Performs an addition operation on the y-values (at each x-value) of the input datasets and returns the result as a new dataset. A minimum of two datasets are expected as input. Extra datasets can be provided optionally. The resultant dataset contains the intersection of x-values from all the input datasets and the summation of the corresponding y-values. (There is no interpolation done for any missing y-values.) If all the input datasets are of the same Quantity type, internal unit conversions are done if needed, and the resultant dataset will also be of the same Quantity type. If any of the input datasets have different Quantity types, no unit conversions are attempted, and the resultant dataset will be Dimensionless. An ArgumentException is thrown if any of the datasets is invalid. An InvalidOperationException is thrown if there is no intersection between the x-values of the input datasets.

member.name: M:Ansys.Mechanical.DataModel.Utilities.Dataset.Operations.Subtraction(Ansys.Mechanical.DataModel.Utilities.Dataset.Dataset2D,Ansys.Mechanical.DataModel.Utilities.Dataset.Dataset2D)
member.summary: Performs a subtraction operation on the y-values of the subtrahend from the minuend and returns the result as a new dataset. The resultant dataset contains the intersection of x-values from all the input datasets and the subtraction of the corresponding y-values. (There is no interpolation done for any missing y-values.) If all the input datasets are of the same Quantity type, internal unit conversions are done if needed, and the resultant dataset will also be of the same Quantity type. If any of the input datasets have different Quantity types, no unit conversions are attempted, and the resultant dataset will be Dimensionless. An ArgumentException is thrown if either one of the datasets is invalid. An InvalidOperationException is thrown if there is no intersection between the x-values of the input datasets.

member.name: M:Ansys.Mechanical.DataModel.Utilities.Dataset.Operations.Multiplication(Ansys.Mechanical.DataModel.Utilities.Dataset.Dataset2D,Ansys.Mechanical.DataModel.Utilities.Dataset.Dataset2D,Ansys.Mechanical.DataModel.Utilities.Dataset.Dataset2D[])
member.summary: Performs a multiplication operation on the y-values (at each x-value) of the input datasets and returns the result as a new dataset. A minimum of two datasets are expected as input. Extra datasets can be provided optionally. The resultant dataset contains the intersection of x-values from all the input datasets and the multiplication of the corresponding y-values. (There is no interpolation done for any missing y-values.) If all the input datasets are of the same Quantity type, internal unit conversions are done if needed, but the resultant dataset will be Dimensionless. An ArgumentException is thrown if either one of the datasets is invalid. An InvalidOperationException is thrown if there is no intersection between the x-values of the input datasets

An ArgumentException is thrown if either one of the datasets is invalid. An InvalidOperationException is thrown if there is no intersection between the x-values of the input datasets.

member.name: M:Ansys.Mechanical.DataModel.Utilities.Dataset.Filters.Butterworth(Ansys.Mechanical.DataModel.Utilities.Dataset.Dataset2D,Ansys.Core.Units.Quantity)
member.summary: Applies Butterworth filter on the given dataset at the given cutoff frequency and returns the result as a new dataset. member.name: T:Ansys.Mechanical.Graphics.Tools.CurrentLegendSettings
member.summary: Represents a CurrentLegendSettings object. This object holds properties of the CurrentLegendSettings.
member.remarks: CurrentLegendSettings operates on the legend of the currently active object. This may require some care when writing scripts, especially in batch mode. Furthermore, CurrentLegendSettings implicitly associates with a given viewport in multi-viewport scenarios. This means that in 4 viewport scenarios it is possible to maintain 4 separate CurrentLegendSettings objects to track the legends for the active object in each viewport independently.
member.example: The following command prints legend statistics for all results in the tree legend = Ansys.Mechanical.Graphics.Tools.CurrentLegendSettings() for res in ExtAPI.DataModel.GetObjectsByType(DataModelObjectCategory.Result): ExtAPI.DataModel.Tree.Activate([res]) low_bound = legend.GetLowerBound(0) high_bound = legend.GetUpperBound(legend.NumberOfBands-1) print('{} has {} legend bands ranging from {} to {}'.format(res.Name, legend.NumberOfBands, low_bound, high_bound))

The following command prints legend statistics for the active object in 2 viewports def dump_legend_stats_for_viewport(viewport_idx): Graphics.ModelViewManager.SetActiveViewPort(viewport_idx) obj = ExtAPI.DataModel.Tree.FirstActiveObject viewport_legend = Ansys.Mechanical.Graphics.Tools.CurrentLegendSettings() low_bound = viewport_legend.GetLowerBound(0) high_bound = viewport_legend.GetUpperBound(viewport_legend.NumberOfBands-1) print('{} has {} legend bands ranging from {} to {}'.format(obj.Name, viewport_legend.NumberOfBands, low_bound, high_bound))
dump_legend_stats_for_viewport(0) dump_legend_stats_for_viewport(1)

member.summary: defines how to import external data from a fixed-width source file.

summary.para: Gets or sets the specified column widths as a `string` using Fortran-esque fixed-format specifications.
This is equivalent to the “User-Defined” format specifier for External Data as described in the product documentation.

Note, however, that regardless of the format specifier all imported columns WILL be interpreted using the .NET command `double.TryParse()` to support the requirements of the underlying variable data for Table.

In the example below, the line has one integer followed by four exponential data types. 385 8.333333333E-003 9.375000000E-003 3.375000000E-001 0.000000000E+000 The corresponding format is `1i3,4e17.9` Where: The first entry is the number of occurrences The second entry is the format specifier The third entry is the number of characters of data in the definition(including numeric values (0-9), the letter 'e' (for instances of scientific notation), and any white space and + or - signs) The fourth entry is the number of digits after the decimal point.
If set to Yes, the data at Midside nodes is calculated as average of data specified at corner nodes.
Defaults to False.
This property is used only when there is another external data file defined with MAPDL import format.

member.summary: Creates a new tag with the given name

member.name: M:Ansys.Mechanical.Application.ObjectTag.attach(Ansys.ACT.Automation.Mechanical.Project)
member.summary: This attach method makes sure the tag is currently in a valid state to attach itself to the UI. Then it record the project given, and transfers itself into an AttachedObjectTag. It does this by taking each object in the detached tag's local list of objects and adding them to the attached tag.
member.remarks: An object tag is in one of two states, attached or detached to the UI and the internal IDSObjectTags objects. If a tag is attached, then every DataModelObject in the Tree that has that tag will reflect it in that specific object's IDSObjectTags. If that object is detached, then no object's IDSObjectTags in the tree will have this tag. Instead, the tag itself will keep track of which objects are a part of the tag with a local list. When a detached tag gets added to the DataModel, it gets attached, iterating through each objects in the tag's local object list, and adding the tag to each DataModelObject's IDSObjectTags.
member.param: The current Data Model's project

member.name: M:Ansys.Mechanical.Application.ObjectTag.detach
member.summary: The detach method first makes sure the tag is in a valid state to become detached, then transforms its internal object _tags into a DetachedTag object, transfering its contents.
member.remarks: For explanation of what being attached/detached means, look at the remarks tag for the attach method.

member.name: P:Ansys.Mechanical.Table.FixedWidthImportSettings.ColumnWidths
member.summary:
Gets or sets the specified column widths. When setting, The value provided to may be either:
A `string` using Fortran-esque fixed-format specifications. This is similar to the “User-Defined” format specifier for External Data as described in the product documentation. Note, however, that regardless of the format specifier all imported columns WILL be interpreted using the .NET command `double.TryParse()` to support the requirements of the underlying variable data for Table.
An containing the widths of each column. Negative values may be specified to define a negated width, meaning ‘-2’ would be equivalent to the fixed-width string specification ’2X’.
member.exception: When the specified value is `null`.
When the specified value is not a supported type.
